abstract: Background: Smooth muscle cells (SMCs) and SMC-derived cells contribute to atherosclerotic plaque stability through matrix production and fibrous cap formation. Recent studies have also identified distinct fibroblast populations in atherosclerotic lesions, but how these populations respond to sustained LDL-C lowering and contribute to plaque remodeling remains poorly understood. Methods: We combined serial histological assessment, SMC lineage tracing, and single-cell RNA sequencing to examine vascular stromal cell and lesion structural responses during 20 weeks of sustained LDL-C lowering in mice with established atherosclerosis. Regulatory network analysis and computational perturbation predictions were supported by KLF3 and FOXD1 silencing in cultured mouse and human aortic fibroblasts. Results: LDL-C lowering led to rapid reductions in macrophage content and cleaved gasdermin D, followed by decreased necrotic core area and increased collagen content and fibrous cap thickness, with minimal change in lesion area. During this remodeling, SMC-derived cell populations changed little. In striking contrast, CD26 and FMOD fibroblast subtypes increased by 5 weeks and remained elevated through 20 weeks, with increased fibroblast-associated signals in the intima and fibrous cap. These populations showed distinct matrix programs, with ECM glycoprotein and regulatory programs enriched in CD26 fibroblasts and collagen and proteoglycan programs in FMOD fibroblasts. Regulatory network analysis identified KLF3 and FOXD1 as candidate master regulators of CD26 and FMOD fibroblasts, respectively. Silencing either factor reduced selected matrix-associated and proliferation transcripts and impaired scratch closure in mouse and human aortic fibroblasts, while KLF3 silencing also increased selected inflammatory genes. Exploratory human genetic analyses identified associations of KLF3-region and FOXD1 variation with coronary artery disease. Conclusions: These findings reveal fibroblast subtype-specific responses during sustained LDL-C lowering and identify KLF3 and FOXD1 as candidate transcriptional regulators of fibroblast matrix-associated and inflammatory functions relevant to plaque remodeling and stabilization.
